second_order: springing fake Destiny reveals and admitting who got caught
theme_note: These codes perform April Fools bait as plausible Destiny news, then expose, praise, complain about, or admit falling for it; the payload varies from registration links and start screens to a Rick Roll and fake ARG.

second_order: swapping the subreddit look and joking through the breakage
theme_note: These codes make or encounter the room's own April Fools styling: the Warframe and Club Penguin swaps, the left sidebar, Gary variants, and members' confusion or bug reports. What varies is whether participants welcome, extend, diagnose, or resist the changed look.

second_order: putting Happy Birthday Norse on the canvas and keeping the joke going
theme_note: These codes carry the room's standing NorseFenrir birthday refrain into canvas inscriptions and back into subreddit exchanges, while participants credit makers, explain the joke, defend or mourn overwritten words, and ask to restore them.

second_order: spotting, sharing, and finding the Destiny work
theme_note: These codes point out, locate, link, or recognize Destiny's canvas marks for people who have not seen them. They range from thin title-only sightings to coordinates, direct links, explanations, and a late recognition of the final art.
These codes count repeated sightings and explain how earlier posts were missed, making repost recognition a small practice distinct from either building or merely finding the art.

second_order: calling Guardians in and showing newcomers how to help
theme_note: These codes recruit helpers, ask them to persist, redirect duplicate proposals toward existing work, explain the pixel rules, and turn people who encounter a partial mark into participants. The calls vary from broad Guardian language to concrete location and participation guidance.

second_order: drawing and revising Destiny marks pixel by pixel
theme_note: These codes do the design work itself: choosing symbols and coordinates, scaling references, placing and correcting pixels, sequencing class emblems, changing plans, and reporting completion. What varies is the mark and whether the proposed build reaches a visible finish.

second_order: keeping the mark clean and fixing overwritten pixels
theme_note: These codes treat a finished or partial mark as continuing work: patching altered pixels, cleaning troll marks, defending the emblem, restoring damaged parts, and persisting despite too few hands. They vary from direct repair reports to renewed calls after damage.

second_order: working out borders, truces, and whether to attack
theme_note: These codes negotiate how Destiny work should coexist with nearby art: proposing treaties, correcting war talk, respecting claimed space, offering reciprocal help, debating attacks, and recounting alliances or threats. Positions vary sharply between fight-back calls, practical doubts, and refusals to vandalize.

second_order: moving live plans to Discord and bringing directions back
theme_note: These codes explicitly route real-time work to #destiny-the-place or the Destiny Discord, credit that venue with organizing, and return invites, coordinates, mock-ups, or status to Reddit. The visible handoff varies while the venue's internal decisions remain unseen.

second_order: celebrating the finish and claiming even one pixel
theme_note: These codes thank builders, claim shared accomplishment, and make contributions from whole designs down to a single possibly wrong pixel count as part of the finish. Celebration varies between collective success, personal pride, and qualified memories of messy construction.
These codes publicly register the canvas ending, once as an edit that interrupts a progress report and once as a later title-only announcement.

second_order: turning the finished drawings into flairs and final images
theme_note: These codes preserve the temporary art after placement ends by cleaning cut-outs, keeping images, petitioning for flairs, working through technical limits, and circulating a final version. The desired afterlife varies between personal archives and subreddit implementation.

second_order: blaming a rival for messing up our place pic
theme_note: This single code preserves one participant's accusation and motive claim; nothing else in the pool establishes the same practice strongly enough to merge it with repair or border negotiation.
